Is a PSARA license valid across all of India? No. It's valid only in the state or Union Territory where it is issued. Operating in a different state requires a separate registration and license there. How many states currently issue PSARA licenses? Every state and Union Territory in India can issue a PSARA license, as all operate under the PSARA framework and have a designated Controlling Authority. However, the actual license volume varies vastly. Some states, like Maharashtra, UP, and some more, have thousands issued, while a couple of Union Territories have zero PSARA licenses issued to date. Do PSARA license fees differ from state to state? Yes. The central government has set a base fee structure (₹5,000 / ₹10,000 / ₹25,000 - depending on the number of cities the agency is operating in), but states have the authority to set their own fees. For example, Karnataka charges more than the central slab. If I already have a PSARA license in one state, can I use it to work in another state? No. You'll need to apply for a fresh license in any other state you want to expand your agency to. You will have to proceed through the registration process from scratch again. Which state currently has the most PSARA-licensed security agencies? According to the latest government data, Maharashtra leads the chart, with over 9,000 PSARA licenses issued to date. Do all states offer online PSARA license applications? Not uniformly. Some states provide the facility of full registration online, while some require some offline visits too. So, it all varies state by state. How long does PSARA license approval typically take? The rule states that the designated controlling authority should proceed with complete approval within 60 days of application completion. The real-world timelines depend on verification speed, inspection scheduling, and how clean your paperwork is. Therefore, it is suggested that you proceed with your application early, having all the paperwork ready beforehand. Is guard training mandatory before I can get a PSARA license? Yes. Your agency needs to implement a credible training program for guards and supervisors. This should be done according to the standards set under the 2020 Model Rules and must be done before your application can be approved. Can a company with foreign shareholders apply for a PSARA license? Yes, a security agency having up to 49% foreign investment is currently permitted to apply for a PSARA license. However, this is subject to applicable FDI conditions and proper disclosure in the application. What happens if I don't renew my PSARA license on time? If you miss the renewal window, your existing license becomes invalid the moment it expires. There's no automatic extension, so track this date carefully. Does the renewal deadline differ by state? Yes, in some cases. The central rule requires filing renewal 45 days before expiry, but Delhi, for instance, requires 90 days. What's the difference between the 2006 Model Rules and the 2020 Rules? The 2006 Central Model Rules were the original detailed operating rules under the PSARA Act. The 2020 Rules replaced them entirely, adding digital processes, electronic background verification through police databases, and more detailed training standards. Can I start deploying guards while my PSARA application is still under review? No. Submitting an application doesn't authorize you to operate. You need the actual license in hand before you can legally provide security services.

Steps to Follow for Expanding:
Starting a security agency in India in 2026 might sound simple on paper. Hire some guards, sign a few contracts, and start earning. Except it isn't that simple, not in India anyway.

Before your agency places a single guard at a client's gate, you need a PSARA license. And here's the part that trips up a lot of new business owners: there is no single "India license" for this. Every state hands out its own. Apply in Punjab, and that license means nothing in Kerala.

This guide walks through the whole picture. Who can apply, what type of license fits your business, how eligibility actually works, how long approval takes, what it costs, and how renewal and rejection work. We'll also cover the PSARA license registration process state by state, as it can differ across different states and regions. If you're planning to grow beyond one city or one state, this is the page to bookmark.
Need the step-by-step application walkthrough with every document listed out? Check our complete PSARA License Registration Guide.
No. This is one thing that many don’t know. Many security agency founders do assume that their one license will apply across any state. But this is where they need to pay attention.

A security agency in Rajasthan doesn't get to walk into Madhya Pradesh and start operating on the strength of its Rajasthan license. Each state (and each Union Territory) has its own Controlling Authority, usually sitting under the Home Department or police setup, and that authority only licenses agencies to work within its own borders.

Think of it less like a driving license and more like a shop license. You don't get to open a branch in another city just because you're registered in your home city. You need fresh permission there too.
So if you're mapping out expansion, plan for separate applications, separate fees, and separate paperwork in every new state. We'll cover how to sequence that later in this guide.

To know why the rules differ across each state, first you should know where these rules come from.
The Private Security Agencies (Regulation) Act, 2005

It is the parent law governing the PSARA registration in India. It was passed by Parliament at that time, owing to the need for legal regulation because private security had grown into a real industry at that time. Security guards were hired more and more by corporate firms, individuals, and societies. There were new security agencies starting everywhere. But alongside that, there was almost no formal oversight of who was running them or who they were hiring. This Act set the basic framework: licensing, eligibility, penalties, and the broad structure every state would follow and build on.
The Original Central Model Rules, 2006

These were the first detailed operating rules under the Act, covering things like how licenses would be processed and what agencies had to do to stay compliant. For over a decade, these model rules were the reference point most states used.
The Central Model Rules Amendment 2020

In 2020, the Ministry of Home Affairs brought the Private Security Agencies Central Model Rules, 2020. This replaced the earlier 2006 rules, and it wasn’t just a small update. This amendment brought in enhanced digital processes to make the process more streamlined with better scrutiny through each step. From electronic background checks through police databases to a detailed training module and guidelines for security guards and supervisors, it set the governance rules for the entire registration, eligibility, and compliance.

Is a PSARA license valid across all of India?
No. It's valid only in the state or Union Territory where it is issued. Operating in a different state requires a separate registration and license there.
How many states currently issue PSARA licenses?

Every state and Union Territory in India can issue a PSARA license, as all operate under the PSARA framework and have a designated Controlling Authority. However, the actual license volume varies vastly. Some states, like Maharashtra, UP, and some more, have thousands issued, while a couple of Union Territories have zero PSARA licenses issued to date.
Do PSARA license fees differ from state to state?

Yes. The central government has set a base fee structure (₹5,000 / ₹10,000 / ₹25,000 - depending on the number of cities the agency is operating in), but states have the authority to set their own fees. For example, Karnataka charges more than the central slab.
If I already have a PSARA license in one state, can I use it to work in another state?
No. You'll need to apply for a fresh license in any other state you want to expand your agency to. You will have to proceed through the registration process from scratch again.
Which state currently has the most PSARA-licensed security agencies?
According to the latest government data, Maharashtra leads the chart, with over 9,000 PSARA licenses issued to date.
Do all states offer online PSARA license applications?
Not uniformly. Some states provide the facility of full registration online, while some require some offline visits too. So, it all varies state by state.
How long does PSARA license approval typically take?

The rule states that the designated controlling authority should proceed with complete approval within 60 days of application completion. The real-world timelines depend on verification speed, inspection scheduling, and how clean your paperwork is. Therefore, it is suggested that you proceed with your application early, having all the paperwork ready beforehand.
